citations.title: Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services: licensure representation and attendant qualifications
citations.requirement: Only a PAS-licensed agency may use or imply the term 'personal assistance services'. Attendants must be 18+ (or a HS graduate/vocational student under 18) and show competency when education or experience does not establish it.

citations.title: Tasks allowed under the PAS category
citations.requirement: Allowed tasks: personal care, RN-delegated or non-delegable health tasks under a written policy meeting 22 TAC Ch. 225, tasks under the HHSC/BON MOU, and physician-delegated tasks (Occ. Code Ch. 157).

citations.title: Operational policies reflect choice and control
citations.requirement: Operational policies must consider individual and family choice and control, functional need, and accessible and flexible services.

citations.title: PAS client file and individualized service plan
citations.requirement: File needs the supervisor's on-site visit documentation and an individualized service plan signed by client/family and agency (services, locations, frequency/duration, start date, charges, supervision plan), plus proof services matched the plan.

citations.title: PAS supervision policy and supervisor qualifications
citations.requirement: Written supervision policy with client/family input on frequency. Supervisor is a licensed nurse or has 2 years of college (1 year of supervisory work may replace each college year). Client-managed programs are exempt from the qualification.

citations.title: G-tube feeding and medication through g-tube
citations.requirement: Unlicensed staff may do g-tube feedings or medication only after training by an RN, physician, PA or qualified trainer: 100% written test, skills checklist, demonstration. Trainer competency is re-evaluated annually.

citations.title: Staffing Policies
citations.requirement: Written staffing policies for employees, volunteers and contractors: orientation, job-specific training and competency, job descriptions, registry/criminal checks, annual evaluations, discipline, volunteers, pediatric competency, signed policy acknowledgment.

citations.title: Verification of Employability: unlicensed employees
citations.requirement: Run a Ch. 250 criminal history check, and search the NAR and EMR before hire or first client contact. Repeat registry searches every 12 months. Give written EMR information. Immediately discharge anyone unemployable or barred.

citations.title: Verification of Employability: unlicensed volunteers
citations.requirement: Criminal history check and NAR/EMR search before a volunteer's first face-to-face client contact. EMR information is due within 5 working days of first contact. Repeat registry searches every 12 months.

citations.title: Employability documentation and arranged services
citations.requirement: Provide compliance documentation to HHSC on request. An agency that gets unlicensed personnel under arrangement from another agency must also meet §558.289(c)-(d).

citations.title: Self-Reported Incidents of Abuse, Neglect, and Exploitation
citations.requirement: Adopt a written policy for reporting abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client by an agency employee. Report within 24 hours to DFPS (1-800-252-5400 or txabusehotline.org) and HHSC (1-800-458-9858).

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness: plan content
citations.requirement: Written all-hazards plan based on a risk assessment. Must name a disaster coordinator and alternate by title and include a continuity-of-operations plan, disaster news monitoring, disaster release of client information, and mitigation/preparedness/response/recovery roles.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness: response, triage, evacuation assistance
citations.requirement: Plan must cover communication modes and contacts, and client triage by service type, continuity need and caregiver availability. Identify clients needing evacuation help and assist with STEAR (2-1-1) registration on request.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness: client information, training, review, drill
citations.requirement: Give and discuss emergency information with each client. Train staff, volunteers and contractors. Review the plan at least annually and after each emergency. Test the response phase in a drill, which can be limited to staff communication.

citations.title: Emergency Preparedness: during-disaster duties, records, HHSC notice, emergency communication system
citations.requirement: Notify HHSC licensing within 5 working days of a temporary relocation or service-area expansion. Administrator and alternate must enroll in HHSC's emergency communication system. Do not recreate damaged records except from electronic copies.

citations.title: Client Conduct and Responsibility and Client Rights: policy, complaint notice, advance notice
citations.requirement: Written rights policy with a no-reprisal grievance mechanism. Follow HRC Ch. 102 for clients 60+. At admission give a written HHSC complaint notice (PO Box 149030, Austin 78714-9030; 1-800-458-9858). Give written rights notice before care.

citations.title: Client Rights enumerated
citations.requirement: Rights include advance information, signed informed consent, participation in and refusal of care, advance notice of expected payment, help understanding rights, respect for person and property, freedom from abuse/neglect/exploitation, confidentiality and grievances without reprisal. Legal representatives may exercise rights.

citations.title: Client Records: system, confidentiality, entries
citations.requirement: Maintain a record system with written procedures for record use, removal and release (release only as allowed by law). Original active records are kept at the place of business. Entries must be signed, dated and corrected by single-line strike-through with date and initials.

citations.title: Client Records: required contents
citations.requirement: Record includes application, service plan per §558.404, progress notes written the day of service and filed within 14 working days, supervisory visit records, and acknowledgments of abuse-reporting policy, complaint instructions, HRC Ch. 102 rights (age 60+) and advance directive notice. Also discharge summary.

citations.title: Client Records: retention
citations.requirement: Written retention policy. Keep original client records at least 5 years after discharge. Do not destroy records tied to unresolved litigation. Arrange preservation of inactive records.

citations.title: Administrator qualifications and conditions (PAS-only)
citations.requirement: Administrator and alternate: HS/GED plus 1 year of experience or training with people with functional disabilities, or 2 years of college in a health field, or the (a)(1) qualifications. Must read, write and understand English, and cannot have a disqualifying Ch. 560 offense. A 12-month bar applies after certain enforcement actions.

citations.title: Initial Educational Training in Administration of Agencies
citations.requirement: First-time administrator and alternate: 24 clock hours within 12 months of designation, with 8 hours in the prior 12 months before designation (licensing standards and listed laws). Presurvey Training does not count. Keep training documentation on file.

citations.title: Continuing Education in Administration of Agencies
citations.requirement: Administrator and alternate each complete 12 hours of continuing education in each 12-month period after the initial training.

citations.title: Financial Solvency and Business Records
citations.requirement: Agency must have sufficient funds to meet payroll and maintain business records (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Prohibition of Solicitation of Patients
citations.requirement: HCSSAs may not solicit clients with payments or other inducements (per fact-checked research). Applies to marketing and referral relationships.

citations.title: License fees
citations.requirement: Initial license $2,625 and renewal $2,625 for three years; $1,750 two-year renewal under current rule, which the 9/18/2026 proposed amendments would delete.

citations.title: Application contents and processing time frames
citations.requirement: Missing application information is due within 30 days of HHSC notice or HHSC may deny and keep the fee. HHSC has up to 45 days to find the application complete and 45 days to issue (§558.31).

citations.title: Obtaining an Initial License
citations.requirement: PAS is one of six license categories. Administrator and alternate must complete HHSC Presurvey Training before applying.

citations.title: Renewal License Application
citations.requirement: Submit renewal by the 45th day before expiration to avoid a late fee. An expired license means the agency must stop operating.

citations.title: Requirements for an Initial Survey
citations.requirement: Admit and serve at least one client, then submit Form 2020 (Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey) within 6 months of the license effective date, listing each client's name, admission date and service category.

citations.title: Contracting Requirements (PHC/CAS/FC)
citations.requirement: HHSC-contracted PHC/CAS/FC providers must comply with Chapter 49 and deliver only personal assistance services under the contract.

citations.title: Attendant Qualifications
citations.requirement: Attendants must meet §558.404 requirements. A parent cannot serve a minor child, a spouse may serve only in Family Care, and 'Do not hire' restrictions apply.

citations.title: Attendant Orientation
citations.requirement: Orient each attendant to the client on or before the first shift and document it on a single form.

citations.title: Referrals and Authorizations
citations.requirement: PHC/CAS provider receives HHSC case worker referrals and must accept all referrals.

citations.title: Pre-Initiation Activities
citations.requirement: Complete the evaluation, service delivery plan and Practitioner's Statement of Medical Need, due within 14 days of a routine referral (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Service Initiation
citations.requirement: For routine PHC/CAS referrals, start services within 7 days after authorization.

citations.title: Service Delivery
citations.requirement: Deliver all authorized and scheduled hours except documented interruptions. Monthly hours may not exceed five times the weekly authorized hours.

citations.title: Supervisory Visits (PHC/CAS/FC)
citations.requirement: Supervisor makes in-person supervisory visits at a frequency the supervisor sets, at least annually, and more often as client needs require.

citations.title: Reimbursement (PHC/CAS/FC)
citations.requirement: Accept HHSC's hourly rate and bill authorized tasks and hours only, in quarter-hour increments (8 minutes or more rounds up).

citations.title: PHC/CAS eligibility and weekly hour limits
citations.requirement: Minimum 6 hours/week (with exceptions). Maximum 42 hours/week for priority clients and 50 hours/week for non-priority clients.

citations.title: Verification of Employability; Annual Search; Discharge
citations.requirement: Employers must verify employability through criminal history and registry searches, repeat the search annually, and discharge anyone found unemployable (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Convictions barring employment (referenced in 26 TAC §558.247)
citations.requirement: Lists convictions that bar employment of unlicensed staff. Convictions not listed must be reviewed and the determination documented under §558.247(a)(2). Statute text itself not fetched.

citations.title: HCSSA definitions and exemptions
citations.requirement: Defines personal assistance services and personal care. Sitter/companion/chore services with no personal care are exempt from licensure (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Rights of the Elderly (referenced in 26 TAC §558.282(c), §558.301(a)(9)(J))
citations.requirement: Agency must comply for clients 60+ and document the client's receipt of a copy of these rights and responsibilities. Statute text itself not fetched.

citations.title: RN Delegation to Unlicensed Personnel (referenced in 26 TAC §558.404(d)(2), (g)(1))
citations.requirement: Agency's written delegation policy and supervision of personnel must comply with the Board of Nursing delegation rules. Chapter text itself not fetched.

citations.cite: 1 TAC Chapter 354, Subchapter O; Tex. Gov't Code §531.024172
citations.title: Electronic Visit Verification
citations.requirement: EVV is required for PHC, CAS, FC, CFC and STAR+PLUS attendant services. Claims must match an accepted EVV visit or the payer denies or recoups them (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: FLSA third-party employment
citations.requirement: Third-party employers such as home care agencies cannot use the companionship or live-in exemptions. Attendants are owed minimum wage and overtime.

citations.cite: U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division, Direct Care Workers: Travel Time
citations.title: Travel time between clients
citations.requirement: Travel between several clients during the workday is compensable hours worked.

citations.title: State responsibilities: screening and enrollment of MCO network providers
citations.requirement: MCO network providers must be screened and enrolled with the state Medicaid agency (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Agency Investigations
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 3 table of contents. Referenced in §558.249(a) for agency investigation of abuse/neglect/exploitation. Text not fetched; confirm requirements before use.

citations.title: Personnel Records
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 3 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm required personnel file contents before use.

citations.title: Administrative and Supervisory Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 3 table of contents. Cross-referenced in §558.256(b)(2). Text not fetched; confirm administrator duties and availability requirements before use.

citations.title: Infection Control
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm infection control policy elements before use.

citations.title: Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm QAPI program requirements before use.

citations.title: Coordination of Services
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the TOC. §558.301(a)(9)(I) requires documentation showing interchange, reporting and coordination of care as required here. Text not fetched.

citations.title: Backup Services and After-Hours Care
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm backup and after-hours requirements before use.

citations.title: Agency and Client Agreement and Disclosure
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm required agreement and disclosure content before use.

citations.title: Time Frame(s) for the Initiation of Care or Services
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm service-initiation time frame requirements before use.

citations.title: Client Transfer or Discharge Notification Requirements
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the TOC. §558.301(a)(9)(N) requires the discharge summary to document the agency's notice to the client and others as required here. Text not fetched.

citations.title: Medication Administration
citations.requirement: Section title confirmed from the Division 4 table of contents. Text not fetched; confirm medication rules before use. PAS attendant medication tasks must also fit §558.404(d)-(h).

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator Responsibilities, and Adoption, Enforcement and Review of Policies
state_specifics: Governing body adopts, implements, enforces and monitors every policy Chapter 558 requires (§558.241 text to be confirmed)
Name an administrator and an alternate by title; both meet §558.244(a)(3) PAS-only qualifications
Administrator duties and availability in §558.243: confirm the rule text before finalizing
Review all policies at least annually. Keep dated revision history and staff re-acknowledgment
Policy manual is available to HHSC surveyors on request

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Administrator and Alternate Administrator Qualifications, Initial Training and Continuing Education
state_specifics: PAS-only: HS diploma/GED plus 1 year of experience or training with people with functional disabilities; or 2 years of full-time college in a health-related field; or home health administrator qualifications
Must read, write and understand English; no disqualifying Ch. 560 offense
HHSC Presurvey Training is completed before applying and does not count toward the 24 hours
First-time administrator and alternate: 24 clock hours within 12 months of designation, with 8 hours in the 12 months before designation
After initial training: 12 hours of continuing education per 12-month period; keep certificates on file

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Licensure, Renewal, Initial Survey, Service Area and Advertising
state_specifics: Hold the HCSSA license with the personal assistance services category; only a PAS-licensed agency may use or imply the term 'personal assistance services'
Initial and three-year renewal fee is $2,625. Missing application information is due within 30 days of HHSC notice or HHSC may deny and keep the fee
Admit and serve at least one client, then file Form 2020 (Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey) within 6 months of the license effective date
Submit renewal in TULIP by the 45th day before expiration. An expired license means the agency must stop operating
Companion/sitter/chore-only services with no personal care are exempt (HSC §142.003(a)(15)); the agency may not advertise or deliver exempt services as personal care

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Staffing Policies: Scope and Signed Policy Acknowledgment
state_specifics: Staffing policies govern all personnel: employees, volunteers and contractors
All direct care staff and staff with direct client contact, employed or contracted, sign a statement that they have read, understand and will comply with agency policies
Signed acknowledgment is kept in the personnel file and renewed when policies change
No state staff-to-client ratio applies to PAS agencies; the agency sets its own staffing levels

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Orientation, Job-Specific Training, Competency and Continuing Training
state_specifics: Orient every employee to agency policies, procedures and objectives before client contact
Job-specific training covers assigned tasks; demonstrate competency when education, license, certification or experience cannot establish it
Continuing, systematic training program with documented in-services
Attendant orientation to each client on or before the first shift, documented on a single form (§277.25)
Training on bloodborne pathogens and infection control before hands-on care

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Job Descriptions, Job Qualifications and Employee Development
state_specifics: Written job description and qualifications for each position: administrator, alternate, client services supervisor, scheduler, attendant
Attendant: 18+ (or HS graduate/vocational student under 18) with competency shown
Supervisor: licensed nurse, or 2 years of college (1 year of supervisory work may replace each college year)
Employee development programs are available to all personnel

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Annual Evaluations, Disciplinary Action and Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Evaluate every employee and volunteer at least annually
Written disciplinary procedures for employees and volunteers
Boundaries: no loans, gifts, financial dealings or personal-relationship exploitation with clients
Immediate discharge when employability checks fail (see ADM-09)

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Volunteers and Contractors
state_specifics: State whether volunteers are used; if so, follow §558.248 (text to be confirmed)
Volunteers: criminal history and NAR/EMR search before first face-to-face client contact; EMR information within 5 working days of first contact; searches repeated every 12 months
Contracted or arranged personnel meet the same staffing and employability standards (§558.247(d))
Volunteers and contractors sign the policy acknowledgment

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Verification of Employability: Criminal History and Registry Checks
state_specifics: Before hire or first client contact: HSC Ch. 250 criminal history check and Nurse Aide Registry (NAR) and Employee Misconduct Registry (EMR) search
Repeat NAR and EMR searches at least every 12 months
Give each employee written EMR information
Immediately discharge anyone unemployable or barred; document review of convictions not listed in HSC §250.006
Provide compliance documentation to HHSC on request

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Personnel Records and Employee Health Screening
state_specifics: Required personnel file contents under §558.246: confirm the rule text before use
File holds application, qualification proof, competency documentation, check/registry results, orientation record, evaluations and signed acknowledgment
Health screening (including TB) at hire and as the agency policy and local health authority require: confirm specific state requirement
Keep personnel records available at the place of business for HHSC review

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Investigating Complaints and Reports of Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation
state_specifics: Written procedures for agency investigation of complaints and reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation (§558.250: confirm text before use)
Name the investigator by title; keep investigation records
Complaints received from clients, families, staff and HHSC go through one log
Cooperate with DFPS and HHSC investigations
No retaliation against a complainant or reporter

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Reporting Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of a Client by an Employee (Self-Reported Incidents)
state_specifics: Written policy for reporting alleged abuse, neglect or exploitation of a client by an agency employee
Report within 24 hours to DFPS (1-800-252-5400 or txabusehotline.org) and HHSC (1-800-458-9858)
Staff are trained on the duty to report and sign acknowledgment of the policy
Document the report, the investigation and the outcome in agency records

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Professional Practice Acts: Reporting and Peer Review
state_specifics: All licensed professionals (such as an RN supervisor) must comply with their practice or title acts on reporting and peer review (§558.251 text to be confirmed)
RN delegation follows 22 TAC Ch. 225
Report suspected practice-act violations to the appropriate licensing board

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Financial Solvency and Business Records
state_specifics: Agency must have sufficient funds to meet payroll
Maintain business records available to HHSC surveyors
Administrator reviews payroll coverage and cash position monthly
Maintain Comptroller and Secretary of State good standing (required for licensing)

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Drug Testing Disclosure
state_specifics: Written policy states whether the agency conducts drug testing of personnel (§558.253 wording to be confirmed)
If testing is done, describe when, how and what happens on a positive result
Provide the policy to applicants and staff

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Accurate Billing and Claims; Corporate Compliance and Fraud Prevention
state_specifics: Bill only for services delivered and authorized, with documentation to support each claim
Medicaid claims must match an accepted EVV visit or the payer denies or recoups them
Bill PHC/CAS/FC in quarter-hour increments (8 minutes or more rounds up)
Staff report suspected fraud to the compliance officer without reprisal
Self-audit billing against service plans and EVV data

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Solicitation of Clients and Marketing
state_specifics: Comply with Texas Occupations Code Ch. 102 on solicitation of patients
No payments or other inducements to solicit clients or referrals
Referral relationships (hospitals, physicians, facilities) are documented and reviewed by the administrator
Advertising uses only services the license permits

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan
state_specifics: Written all-hazards plan based on a risk assessment; name disaster coordinator and alternate by title
Review at least annually and after each emergency; test the response phase in a drill (may be limited to staff communication)
Identify clients needing evacuation help; assist with STEAR (2-1-1) registration on request
Give and discuss emergency information with each client; train all staff, volunteers and contractors
Notify HHSC licensing within 5 working days of temporary relocation or service-area expansion; administrator and alternate enroll in HHSC emergency communication system

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 3 – Agency Administration (§§558.241–558.260)
policies.title: Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: QAPI program requirements in §558.287: confirm rule text before use
Track missed visits, incidents, complaints, EVV exceptions and supervisory-visit timeliness
Review results at least annually with the governing body
Document corrective actions and follow-up

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility, Initial Assessment and Reassessment
state_specifics: Supervisor makes an on-site visit before service to assess needs and the home environment
Medicaid PHC/CAS: minimum 6 hours/week (with exceptions); maximum 42 hours/week priority and 50 hours/week non-priority
Reassess at supervisory visits and on any change in condition
Accept clients only when the agency can safely meet the identified needs
Client records the intake documentation

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Start of Care, Placing Services on Hold, Transfer and Discharge
state_specifics: Written criteria for start of care, hold, transfer and discharge
Client transfer/discharge notice requirements are in §558.295: confirm text before use
Discharge summary is placed in the client record and documents notice to the client and others
Notify the MCO service coordinator or HHSC case worker when a Medicaid client is held, transferred or discharged
Safe-transition steps for clients who still need care

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Time Frames for Initiation of Care or Services
state_specifics: Written policy sets the time frame for initiating care (§558.294: confirm text)
PHC/CAS routine referrals: evaluation, service delivery plan and Practitioner's Statement of Medical Need within 14 days; start services within 7 days after authorization
Document the start date in the service plan
Tell the client or referral source promptly if the agency cannot start on time

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Care Planning
state_specifics: Individualized service plan from the supervisor's on-site visit, signed by client/family and agency
Plan lists services, locations, frequency/duration, start date, charges and supervision plan
Update the plan on change in need and at each supervisory visit
Keep proof services delivered matched the plan

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Emergencies in the Home and Triage of Clients in a Disaster
state_specifics: Attendant calls 911 first for life-threatening emergencies, then notifies the supervisor and family/representative
Attendants do not give medical treatment beyond first aid
Disaster triage ranks clients by service type, continuity need and caregiver availability
Keep a current list of clients needing evacuation help; assist with STEAR (2-1-1) registration on request
Document each emergency on an incident report

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Safety of Staff, Workplace Violence and Client Transportation
state_specifics: Attendants may leave an unsafe home and report immediately to the supervisor
Report threats, violence, unsafe conditions, pets and weapons concerns
Safe-lifting and body-mechanics training; PPE supplied
Transporting clients only if authorized in the service plan, with a valid license and insurance
Travel between clients in an attendant's own vehicle is compensable time under the FLSA

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Procedures Staff Will and Will Not Perform
state_specifics: Permitted tasks: personal care and RN-delegated or non-delegable health tasks under written policy (22 TAC Ch. 225), tasks under the HHSC/BON MOU, and physician-delegated tasks (Occ. Code Ch. 157)
Attendants perform no sterile or skilled procedures such as dressing changes, Foley catheter changes or wound irrigation
G-tube feedings only after the training in §558.404(h)
Task list is printed in the service plan and the attendant orientation form
Questions about a task go to the supervisor before the task is done

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Skilled Services Not Provided: Intravenous Services, Psychiatric Nursing, Physician Orders and Waived Testing
state_specifics: Agency does not provide IV services, psychiatric nursing procedures, or waived testing under its PAS-only scope
Agency does not receive or carry out physician orders except for physician-delegated tasks allowed by §558.404(d)
Clients needing these services are referred to a licensed home health agency
Staff who are asked to do these services decline and notify the supervisor

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Care of the Pediatric Client
state_specifics: Policy states whether the agency serves clients under 18
If served, attendants show pediatric competency (§558.245) and a parent or guardian is involved in the service plan
In CAS a parent cannot serve as attendant for a minor child
Report suspected abuse or neglect of a child to DFPS (1-800-252-5400)

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client and Caregiver Teaching, Coordination of Care and Other Client Care Matters
state_specifics: Attendants give no disease-process teaching; they reinforce instructions from the client's licensed providers and refer questions to the supervisor
Coordination-of-care rules are in §558.288: confirm text before use
Document interchange, reporting and coordination of care in the client record (§558.301(a)(9)(I))
Coordinate with the MCO service coordinator, HHSC case worker and other providers
Other client care matters not listed are decided by the administrator and recorded

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Care of a Client with a Terminal Illness or Terminal Prognosis
state_specifics: Agency provides personal care only; hospice or home health provides clinical and palliative care
Coordinate with hospice team and follow the client's advance directives
Update the service plan as needs change and increase supervisory contact
Attendants report changes in condition to the supervisor immediately

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Medication Assistance, Self-Administration Support and Medication Monitoring
state_specifics: Attendants may remind and assist with self-administered medications as allowed by §558.404(d); medication rules in §558.300: confirm text before use
Any medication task beyond that requires RN delegation under 22 TAC Ch. 225 or physician delegation
Medication through a g-tube only after training under §558.404(h)
Attendants report refusals, side effects, errors and missed doses to the supervisor the same day
Document assistance in the progress note

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client Rights, Conduct and Responsibility; Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Written rights policy with a grievance mechanism the client can use without fear of reprisal
Give written notice of the policy before care begins or at the initial evaluation visit
At admission give the written HHSC complaint notice (PO Box 149030, Austin 78714-9030; 1-800-458-9858)
Clients 60+ also receive HRC Ch. 102 rights, with receipt documented
Legal representatives may exercise client rights

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Respect for client person and property is a stated client right
Staff may not accept gifts, loans or money, serve as agent or beneficiary, or handle client finances beyond approved errands with receipts
Allegations of exploitation are reported to DFPS (1-800-252-5400) and HHSC (1-800-458-9858) within 24 hours
Report any property loss to the supervisor immediately

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Advance Directives
state_specifics: Written policy implementing advance directives under Health & Safety Code Ch. 166 (§558.283 text to be confirmed)
State clearly any procedure the agency is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold
Give clients written notice of the policy; record receipt in the client file
Attendants call 911 unless a valid out-of-hospital DNR order is presented

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Policies prevent the spread of infectious and communicable disease and comply with HSC Ch. 81, the OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and HSC Ch. 85, Subchapter I (§558.285 text to be confirmed)
Document infections a client acquires while receiving services
Hand hygiene, PPE, sharps and exposure-incident procedures
Attendants with symptoms of communicable illness stay off client visits

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Backup Services, Missed Visits and After-Hours Care
state_specifics: Written policy ensures backup services when an employee or contractor is unavailable (§558.290: confirm current text)
Administrator or alternate available during operating hours; after-hours on-call number given to every client
Missed visits trigger a replacement attendant and notice to the client
Medicaid: deliver all authorized, scheduled hours except documented interruptions

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Agency Dissolution Contingency Plan and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Written contingency plan on dissolution to assure continuity of client care; consistent with §558.295 and §558.217 (§558.291 text to be confirmed)
Notify clients, payers and HHSC and arrange transfers to other providers
Arrange preservation of client records after closure
Retain original client records at least 5 years after discharge

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Agency-client agreement and disclosure content in §558.292: confirm text before use
Service plan lists charges when the client pays in whole or in part
Give advance notice of expected payment, in writing, before care
Explain charges, minimum visit lengths and changes in rate in plain language

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client Record System: Use, Removal and Release of Information
state_specifics: Written procedures for use and removal of records, release of information and incorporating notes into the record
Release only as allowed by law
Original active records are kept at the place of business
Entries are signed and dated; corrections use a single-line strike-through with date and initials
Progress notes are written the day of service and filed within 14 working days

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Client Records: Contents and Retention
state_specifics: Written retention policy; keep original client records at least 5 years after discharge
Do not destroy records tied to unresolved litigation
Arrange preservation of inactive records

Record contents: application, service plan, progress notes, supervisory visit records, signed acknowledgments (abuse reporting, complaint instructions, HRC Ch. 102, advance directive notice) and discharge summary

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Confidentiality is a stated client right under §558.282
Release client information only as allowed by law
Disaster release of client information is part of the emergency plan
Designate a privacy officer; train staff at orientation and annually; report breaches

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964
state_specifics: Serve clients without discrimination in admission, care or discharge
Provide interpreter and communication aids at no charge
Give rights notices in a language and format the client understands
Policies reflect accessible and flexible services (§558.404(e))

policies.category: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: Attendants report falls, injuries, emergencies, property loss and client refusals to the supervisor the same day
Written incident report is completed and reviewed by the administrator
Abuse, neglect or exploitation by an employee is reported to DFPS and HHSC within 24 hours
Incidents feed the QAPI review

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Use of the Term 'Personal Assistance Services' and Permitted Task Scope
state_specifics: Only a PAS-licensed agency may use or imply the term 'personal assistance services'
Allowed tasks: personal care; RN-delegated or non-delegable health tasks; tasks under the HHSC/BON MOU; physician-delegated tasks
Personal care includes bathing, dressing, grooming, feeding, toileting, positioning, transfers and self-administered medications
Services without personal care (sitter, companion, chore) are outside licensure

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Health-Related Tasks by Unlicensed Personnel and RN Delegation
state_specifics: Written policy adopted, implemented and enforced for health-related tasks that an RN may delegate or determines do not need delegation, in compliance with 22 TAC Ch. 225
RN assesses the client, delegates task by task and trains and supervises the attendant
Attendants do not perform a health-related task without delegation or documentation that none is needed
Delegation records are in the client file

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Individual and Family Choice and Control; Functional Need; Accessible and Flexible Services
state_specifics: All operational policies consider individual and family choice and control, functional need, and accessible and flexible services
Clients choose or help choose schedule, attendant and how tasks are done within the service plan
Clients can request an attendant change
Record client preferences in the service plan

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Individualized Service Plan and PAS Client File
state_specifics: File holds documentation of the supervisor's on-site visit
Individualized service plan signed by client/family and agency
Plan lists services, locations, frequency and duration, start date, charges and supervision plan
File includes proof that services delivered matched the plan

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Supervision of Personnel, Supervisory Visits and Supervisor Qualifications
state_specifics: Written supervision policy, in addition to staffing policies, with client or family input on supervision frequency
Supervision follows agency policy, state law and 22 TAC Ch. 225
Supervisor: licensed nurse, or 2 years of college (1 year of supervisory work may replace each college year); client-managed programs exempt
PHC/CAS/FC: in-person supervisory visits at a frequency the supervisor sets, at least annually

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: G-Tube Feeding and Medication Through a G-Tube
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff do g-tube feeding or medication only after training by an RN, physician, PA or qualified trainer
Training includes a 100% written test, skills checklist and demonstration
Trainer competency is re-evaluated annually
Agency states in policy whether it offers this task; if not, staff decline

policies.category: Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services
policies.title: Attendant Qualifications and Orientation to Each Client
state_specifics: Attendant is 18+ (or an HS graduate/vocational student under 18) with competency shown where education or experience does not establish it
Orient each attendant to the client on or before the first shift; document on a single form
Medicaid: attendant meets §558.404; a parent cannot serve a minor child; a spouse serves only in Family Care; 'Do not hire' restrictions apply
Complete employability checks before assignment

policies.category: Medicaid Programs, EVV and Payers
policies.title: HHSC PHC/CAS/Family Care Contract Requirements, Referrals, Service Delivery and Reimbursement
state_specifics: Accept all HHSC case worker referrals; comply with Ch. 49; deliver only personal assistance services under the contract
Evaluation, service delivery plan and Practitioner's Statement of Medical Need within 14 days of a routine referral; start within 7 days after authorization
Deliver all authorized, scheduled hours except documented interruptions; monthly hours may not exceed 5 times the weekly authorized hours
Weekly hours: minimum 6 (with exceptions); maximum 42 priority and 50 non-priority
Accept HHSC's hourly rate; bill only authorized tasks and hours in quarter-hour increments (8 minutes or more rounds up)

policies.category: Medicaid Programs, EVV and Payers
policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV required for PHC, CAS, FC, CFC and STAR+PLUS attendant services
Use the state's free EVV system (HHAeXchange) or an approved proprietary system
Attendants clock in and out at the client's location; supervisor corrects visit maintenance before billing
Claims must match an accepted EVV visit (Medicaid ID, date, NPI, HCPCS, modifiers, units) or the payer denies or recoups them

policies.category: Medicaid Programs, EVV and Payers
policies.title: STAR+PLUS and CFC Coordination, Medicaid Enrollment and Payer Credentialing
state_specifics: MCO network providers are screened and enrolled with the state Medicaid agency
MCO service coordinators authorize PAS and CFC; the agency holds a network contract with each MCO
Provide only authorized services; notify the service coordinator of changes in condition, missed visits and discharge
Verify each MCO's contract rate; payment rates in effect since 9/1/2025
Client rights and HCBS settings requirements apply to Medicaid HCBS clients

policies.category: Wage and Hour Compliance
policies.title: Wage, Hour, Overtime and Travel-Time Compliance
state_specifics: As a third-party employer the agency cannot use the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions; attendants are owed minimum wage and overtime
Travel between clients during the workday is compensable hours worked
Texas minimum wage is $7.25/hour, equal to the federal rate
Payroll records show hours worked, including travel, orientation and training time
Workers' compensation is elective for Texas private employers

documents.title: Licensing Standards for Home and Community Support Services Agencies – the Chapter 558 sections that require written policies (§§558.241, .245, .249, .250, .251, .253–.256, .281–.283, .285, .290–.292, .294, .301, .404). Texas has no single policy checklist, so these sections are used instead.
documents.form_number: 26 TAC Chapter 558 (no HHSC policy-checklist form exists)
documents.issuer: Texas HHSC, Long-term Care Regulation (HCSSA Licensing)
documents.version: Current Texas Administrative Code as published by Cornell LII. §558.404 and §558.521 show amendments effective 4/25/2021. HHSC proposed further amendments to §§558.245, .249, .250, .256, .281, .288 and .290 in the 9/18/2026 Texas Register; I saw no adoption notice, so confirm the final text before submitting.
documents.how_used:
HHSC says the Chapter 558 regulations dictate the required policies and that HHSC does not maintain a list of required HCSSA policies.
 I therefore used the rule sections that list written policies. §558.404 is the PAS-category section, and §558.521(d)(3) requires all policies to be available at the initial survey.

documents.title: HCSSA Pre-Survey Computer-Based Training, Module 2 (HHSC's plain-language summary of the Chapter 558 policy requirements)
documents.how_used: Used only for the wording of the §558.245 staffing-policy elements and for the dissolution and infection-control items. Its text is HHSC's summary, not the rule text.

documents.title: HCSSA Frequently Asked Questions
documents.how_used: Confirms that no state policy checklist exists and that Chapter 558 is the source of the required policies.

required_items.text: When developing its operational policies, the agency must make them considerate of individual and family choice and control, functional need, and accessible and flexible services.

Written policy, adopted, implemented and enforced, on health-related tasks done by unlicensed personnel that an RN may delegate or determines do not need delegation, in compliance with 22 TAC Chapter 225.

Written policy, in addition to the §558.245 staffing policies, addressing supervision of personnel with input from the client or family on the frequency of supervision.
 Supervisor qualifications are in §558.404(g)(2). Under §558.404(g)(1), supervision must follow agency policy, state law and 22 TAC Chapter 225.
Written staffing policies that govern all personnel used by the agency, including employees, volunteers, and contractors.
Requirements for orientation to the policies, procedures, and objectives of the agency.

Requirements for participation by all personnel in job-specific training. Training policies must ensure personnel are oriented to tasks and show competency when it cannot be determined through education, license, certification or experience (b)(2)(A)-(B). They must also ensure a continuing systematic training program (b)(2)(C).
Address participation by all personnel in appropriate employee development programs.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.245(b) (sub-paragraph number not verified; wording from HHSC CBT Module 2)

required_items.text: Include a written job description and job qualifications for each position at the agency.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.245(b) (sub-paragraph number not verified; wording from HHSC CBT Module 2)

required_items.text: Include procedures for processing criminal history checks and searches of the nurse aide registry and the employee misconduct registry for unlicensed personnel (see §558.247).
Ensure annual evaluation of employee and volunteer performance.
Address employee and volunteer disciplinary action and procedures.
Address use of volunteers, if volunteers are used (see §558.248).

Include a requirement that all direct care staff and staff with direct client contact, whether employed or contracted, sign a statement that they have read, understand and will comply with all applicable agency policies.
The license holder must adopt, implement, enforce and monitor agency policies required by Chapter 558.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.241 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text: Written policy on the agency's procedures for investigating complaints and reports of abuse, neglect and exploitation.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.243 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text: Written policy on procedures for reporting alleged acts of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of a client by an employee of the agency.
Written policy on the agency's procedures for investigating complaints and reports of abuse, neglect, and exploitation. The policy must meet the requirements of §558.250.
Written policy ensuring all professional disciplines comply with their practice acts or title acts on reporting and peer review.

Written policy describing whether the agency conducts drug testing (disclosure of drug testing policy).
 The cited source text is truncated; confirm the wording in the rule.
Written policy ensuring the agency submits accurate billings and insurance claims.
Written policy ensuring compliance with Texas Occupations Code Chapter 102 on solicitation of patients.

A written emergency preparedness and response plan based on a risk assessment.
 
The plan must be reviewed internally at least annually and after each actual emergency response, and its response phase tested in a planned drill if not tested in an actual emergency.

Initial assessment, reassessment.
 Elements (1)-(16) of the client care policy are required only if covered under the agency's scope of services.
Start of care, placing services on hold, transfer, and discharge.
Intravenous services.
Care of the pediatric client.
Triaging clients in the event of disaster.
How to handle emergencies in the home.
Safety of staff.
Procedures the staff will perform for clients, such as dressing changes, Foley catheter changes, wound irrigation, administration of medication.
Psychiatric nursing procedures.
Patient and caregiver teaching relating to disease process/procedures.
Care planning.
Care of a client who has a terminal illness or a terminal prognosis.
Receiving physician orders.
Performing waived testing.
Medication monitoring.
Anything else pertaining to client care.

Written policy governing client conduct and responsibility and client rights, including a grievance mechanism under which a client can participate without fear of reprisal.
 
Before care begins, or at the initial evaluation visit, the client or legal representative must receive written notice of all these policies (§558.282(e)).

Written policy on implementing advance directives, in compliance with Health and Safety Code Chapter 166. It must clearly state any procedure the agency is unwilling or unable to provide or withhold.
 
Clients must be given written notice of the policy.
required_items.cite: 26 TAC §558.283 (summary from industry training handout; confirm in the rule text)

required_items.text:
Written infection control policies, including preventing the spread of infectious and communicable disease. They must ensure compliance with Health and Safety Code Chapter 81, the OSHA bloodborne pathogens rule, and Health and Safety Code Chapter 85, Subchapter I.
 
They must require documentation of infections a client acquires while receiving services.

Written policy ensuring backup services are available when an employee or contractor is not available to deliver services. The only text I found for this section is HHSC's description of its proposed amendment. 
The proposal clarifies the written-policy requirement for ensuring backup services.
 Confirm the current text.
Written policy describing the agency's contingency plan, to be implemented on dissolution to assure continuity of client care. It must be consistent with §558.295 and comply with §558.217.
Written policy establishing time frame(s) for the initiation of care.
Written procedures on the use and removal of records, the release of information, and, when applicable, incorporating notes into the client record.
Written policy on retention of records; original client records must be kept at least five years after discharge.

sections: Subchapter C, Division 4 – Provision and Coordination of Treatment Services (§§558.281–558.303)
Subchapter D – §558.404 Standards Specific to Agencies Licensed to Provide Personal Assistance Services

official.notes: Texas has no policy checklist form for HCSSA-PAS. HHSC's FAQ says Chapter 558 dictates the required policies and that HHSC keeps no list. Policies are not submitted with the Form 2021 application. They are reviewed on-site at the initial survey: within 6 months of licensure the agency must admit at least one client and submit Form 2020 (Notification of Readiness for Initial Survey). At the survey the agency must have all agency policies required by Chapter 558, client records and personnel records ready for the surveyor (§558.521(a)-(d)). Organize the manual to follow the rule order above: Division 3 administration and staffing, Division 4 client care, rights and records, then PAS-specific §558.404, with section numbers cited in each policy so a surveyor can match policy to rule. For PAS, §558.281 elements apply only if within the agency's scope of services. The 558.404(e) policy principles (individual and family choice and control, functional need, accessible and flexible services) apply to all operational policies. Also include a client-file template for the §558.404(f) individualized service plan, which must be signed by the client or family and the agency. §558.404(f)(2)(A)-(F) lists what it must contain. The 9/18/2026 Texas Register proposals would change §§558.245 (registry searches), 558.249, 558.250, 558.256, 558.281, 558.288 and 558.290. They also add a new §558.251 on reporting abuse, neglect and exploitation and a workplace-violence policy for agencies with 2+ nurses, which does not apply to PAS-only agencies. Re-check the TAC before finalizing. I could not retrieve the full current text of these sections, so check them directly against the rule: 558.243 (complaint/ANE procedures), 558.247 and 558.248 (employability checks, volunteers), 558.253, 558.287 (QAPI), 558.288 (coordination of services), 558.289 (contractors), 558.292 (agency-client agreement and disclosure), 558.295 (transfer/discharge notice) and 558.300 (medication administration). For the 558.245(b) elements beyond (b)(1)-(2), I took the wording from HHSC's CBT summary and could not verify the sub-paragraph numbers. Separate Medicaid contracting requirements (26 TAC Chapter 277 for PHC/CAS/FC, MCO credentialing, EVV) were not reviewed here.
